Phosphine-catalyzed [3 + 2] annulation of 2-aminoacrylates with 
allenoates and mechanistic studies
Xiao-Yun Wu,a Hou-Ze Gui,a Harish Jangra,d Yin Wei,*b Hendrik Zipse,*d and Min Shi*a,b,c
A convenient and efficient strategy for the synthesis of 3-pyrrolines containing an amino quaternary stereogenic center via 
phosphine-catalyzed formal [3 + 2] annulation of allenoates with 2-aminoacrylates is disclosed. A wide range of substrates 
underwent this reaction smoothly, affording a series of 3-pyrrolines in good to excellent yields; and it could be extended to 
a gram-scale reaction.  The kinetic profiles and the calculated Methyl Anion Affinity (MAA) values were employed to 
explain the reactivites of different allenoates used in the reaction, which provides the deep understanding for the catalytic 
mechanism of this type of reaction.
Introduction
Pyrrolines and their derivatives represent an important class 
of heterocycles, which often exist in nature products and 
therapeutic compounds.[1] 3-Pyrroline-containing compounds 
possess many important biological activities including 
inhibitory activity against monoamine oxidase (MAO),[2] 
agonist activity at the NMDA receptor,[3] anticancer activity,[4] 
and protein GGTase-I inhibitors (shown in Fig. 1).[5] Owing to 
their pharmaceutical interest and synthetic utility, many 
methods have been developed for the synthesis of 3-pyrroline-
containing compounds.[6] Nucleophilic phosphine organocatalzed 
[3+2] cycloaddition reaction has become one of important synthetic 
methods for the construction of five-membered-ring systems in 
recent years, since Lu’s pioneer work on phosphine-catalyzed [3 + 2] 
cycloaddition of allenoates and activated alkenes or imines was 
reported.[7] Although phosphine-catalyzed [3 + 2] cycloaddition of 
allenoates and electron-deficient olefins or imines attract great 
interests for researchers in expanding its scope, [8] there are rare 
reports on [3 + 2] cycloaddition reactions using ketimines as 
substrates, which is probably due to their steric hinderance, 
intrinsic low reactivity. [9] As far as we know, there are only several 
reports[10] about phosphine-catalyzed [3 + 2] cycloadditions of 
allenoates and ketimines (shown in Scheme 1). For instance, Ye’s 
group explored phosphine-catalyzed [3 + 2] cycloaddition of 
allenoates and cyclic ketimines. [10a] Ma and co-workers have 
successfully synthesized the fluorinated 3-pyrrolines by using 
phosphine-catalyzed cycloadditions of allenoates with electron-
deficient olefins and imines. [10b] In this context, we have an interest 
in using a new type of ketoimine species in common phosphine-
catalyzed annulation reactions to construct 3-pyrrolines and their 
derivatives.

In 2017, Qi’s group reported an enantioselective synthesis of 
γ-lactam derivatives via a NHC-catalyzed [3 + 2] annulation of 
enals and 2-aminoacrylates.[11] Moreover, our group previously 
reported the synthesis of spirothioureas having an amino 
quaternary stereogenic center via amine-catalyzed [3 + 2] 
annulation of 3-isothiocyanato oxindoles and 2-aminoacrylates 
in 2018.[12] We assume that using such kind of in-situ 
generated ketoimine intermediate[13] can construct an amino 
quaternary stereogenic center via phosphine-catalyzed 
cycloaddition. Encouraged by these results and our continuous 
efforts on exploring the utilities of phosphine-catalyzed 
cycloaddition,[14] we envisaged that we could synthesize 3-
pyrrolines through phosphine-catalyzed cycloaddition of 2-
aminoacrylates with allenoates (Scheme 1).

Results and discussion
The phosphine-catalyzed reaction of 2-aminoacrylate 1a 
with allenoate 2a was chosen as the model system to optimize 
the reaction conditions. The results showed in Table 1. Initially, 
2-aminoacrylate (1a, 1.0 equiv) was treated with allenoate (2a, 
1.2 equiv) and PPh3 (0.1 equiv) in 1,4-dioxane at room 
temperature for 4 h under an argon atmosphere. The desired 
product 3aa was only obtained in trace amount (Table 1, entry 
1). Subsequently, several solvents (PhMe, CH3CN, THF, CDCl3, 
DCM) were screened (Table 1, entries 2-6); the results showed 
that using THF as solvent gave the best efficiency in terms of 
product yield up to 92%. Furthermore, catalyst screening 
showed that PPh3 was the most efficient catalyst for this 
reaction (Table 1, entries 7-10). Using PBu3 as a catalyst, a 
cascade dimerization and cyclization of 1a could take place.[15] 
Changing the ratio of 1a and 2a from 1:2 to 2:1 led to the 
production of 3aa in a slightly decreased yield (Table 1, entries 
11-12). Then, adding 2 equiv of base Cs2CO3 did not affect the 
yield significantly (Table 1, entry 13). In the absence of PPh3, 
the reaction could not take place (Table 1, entry 14).

With the optimized reaction conditions in hand, we first 
investigated the substrate scope of this phosphine-catalyzed 
[3+2] annulation of allenoate 2a with a variety of 2-
aminoacrylates, and the results are summarized in Table 2. 2-
aminoacrylates bearing electron-donating substituents at the 
phenyl ring including alkyl groups (substrates 1a, 1b and 1f), 
alkoxy group (substrate 1c) as well as no substituent (substrate 
1e) reacted smoothly, giving the desired products (3aa, 3ba, 
3fa, 3ca, 3ea) in yield ranging from 70% to 92%. However, 2-
aminoacrylates (substrates 1h, 1i, 1j, 1k, 1l, 1m, 1n, except for 
1g) bearing electron-withdrawing substituents on the benzene 
ring significantly affected the reaction, leading to the yields 
dropping; the corresponding products 3ha, 3ia, 3ja, 3ka, 3la, 
3ma, 3na were accessed in moderate yields ranging from 42%

to 70%. The substrate 1d having methylsulfonyl group as 
protecting group underwent this reaction smoothly, affording 
the product 3da in 75% yield. However, no reaction took place 
when the substrate’s protecting group was replaced by acyl 
protecting groups such as Ac and Boc. Besides the arene 
sulfonyl groups, the sulfonyl groups containing heterocycle 
such as thiophene (substrate 1o) and 5-methylpyridine 
(substrate 1p) have been proved to be compatible, and 
generated the desired products (3oa, 3pa) in yields of 50% and 
80%, respectively. Moreover, no reactions took place when 2-
aminoacrylates[16] with β-substitutions (1q, 1r) were used. 
Subsequently, the reactions of several representative 2-
aminoacrylates having sulfonyl protecting group containing 
methyl, butyl, alkoxy and trifluoromethyl of with other 
allenoates (2b, 2c, 2d) were investigated. The reactions of 2-
aminoacrylates containing electron-donating groups with alkyl 
allenoates (substrates 2b, 2d) and phenyl allenoate (substrate 
2c) proceeded smoothly, affording the corresponding products 
3ab, 3bb, 3cb, 3ac, 3bc, 3cc, 3ad; their yields were similar to 
those products obtained from allenoate 2a. The reactions of 2-
aminoacrylates containing electron-withdrawing groups with 
allenoates (2b, 2c) gave the desired products 3db, 3ec, whose 
yields increased compared with the product 3ma. Next, in 
order to evaluate the effect of ester groups in substrates 1 on 
the reaction, the methyl ester was displaced by ethyl ester 
(substrate 1n), and benzyl ester (substrate 1o). The 
corresponding reaction of 1n with 2a gave an excellent yield of 
86% for product 3an. The substrate 1o reacted with benzyl 
(substrate 2a), alkyl (substrate 2b) and phenyl allenoate 
(substrate 2c), providing the expected products 3ao, 3eb, 3fc 
in 80-94% yields. In addition, it is regrettable that γ-substituted 
allenoates (2e, 2f) did not react with 1a under the standard 
conditions.
To further demonstrate the benefits of employing 
phosphine catalysis in [3 + 2] annulation, the enantioselective 
variant was explored (for details, see Supporting Information). 
A series of bifunctional chiral phosphine organocatalysts were 
tested for this reaction. Thiourea-derived chiral catalysis L was 
found to provide the product 3aa’ in excellent yield with 
moderate enantioselectivity (92% yield and 52% ee., Scheme 
2). We also attempted the asymmetric reactions of 1a with 2c; 
unfortunately, an excellent enantioselectivity was not 
achieved (for details, see Supporting Information).

To demonstrate the synthetic utility of the 3-pyrroline 
products 3, some transformations and a large-scale production 
were performed (Scheme 3). Hydrogenation of 3-pyrroline 3aa 
could take place catalyzed by Pd/C, affording carboxylic acid 4a 
in excellent yield and diastereoselectivity (more than 20:1 dr 
value). The structure of 4a was assigned by X-ray diffraction 
(Fig. 2). On the other hand, in the presence of strong base, the 
debenzylation of 3aa was easy to occur, producing pyrrole-
fused-carboxylic acid 4b in yield of 56%. In addition, to 
demonstrate the scalability of this phosphine-catalyzed [3 + 2] 
cycloaddition reaction, we carried out the model reaction on a 
12 mmol scale to provide the expected product 3aa in 83% 
yield (Scheme 3b). This demonstrated that our methodology 
could be potentially scaled up to gram-scale synthesis.

Based on the commonly accepted mechanism for 
phosphine-catalyzed cycloaddition reaction, the proposed 
reaction mechanism is shown in Scheme 4. The cycloaddition 
reaction is initiated by the in situ generated zwitterionic 
intermediate I through the addition of a tertiary phosphine to 
the allenoate 2a. The intermediate I acts as a 1,3-dipole and 
undergoes a nucleophilic addition with in situ generated 
ketoimine intermediate 1a’ via tautomerization of 2-
aminoacrylate 1a to give a phosphorus ylide II. Next, the ylide 
II completes a cycloaddition to form an intermediate III, which 
subsequently undergoes a formal [1,2]-proton shift to yield 
intermediate IV and followed by an elimination process to 
afford cycloaddition product 3aa.

In a recent report,[17] it was shown that the calculated 
Methyl Anion Affinity (MAA) values can serve as indicators of 
the electrophilicities of Michael acceptors. We would like to 
investigate whether there are some correlations between the 
calculated MAA values and the reactivities of allenoates in this 
type of cycloaddition reaction; thus, a series of time-
dependent NMR studies were carried out. The reactions of 1a 
with several allenoates 2a, 2b and 2c were tested in the 
presence of the 10 mol% or 30 mol% of PPh3 in CDCl3, 
respectively. The kinetic profiles were shown in Fig. 3 and Fig. 
4 (for details, see Supporting Information). The experimental 
results were consistent with the calculation results (Fig. 5). The 
benzyl 2,3-butadienoate (substrate 2a), having the smallest 
MAA value, demonstrated the lowest reaction rate. The kinetic 
curves of ethyl 2,3-butadienoate (substrate 2b) also fit the 
calculation results as well. Moreover, phenyl 2,3-butadienoate 
(substrate 2c) having the largest MAA value demonstrated the 
fastest reaction rate among the tested allenoates. These 
findings indicate that the calculated MAA values can serve as 
indicators for the reactivities of allenoates in this cycloaddition 
reaction, which may help the further development for this 
type of reaction. It should be mentioned that the turnover 
curves in Figs. 3 and 4 are in agreement with the situation of 
"pre-steady state kinetics" often seen in multistep catalytic 
sequences.[18] These schemes are characterized by very fast 
initial product formation (boost phase) for the very first 
turnover cycle of the catalyst, and subsequent slowdown due 
to a decrease in the concentration of free catalyst. It is very 
nicely seen for the turnover curves for 2c, whose first point (at 
2 min) on the turnover curves in Fig. 3 and 4 correspond 
effectively to the catalyst concentrations. The situation is 
really different for allenoate 2a. The reaction of 2a appears to 
get faster at lower catalyst concentration. This interesting 
result may indicate that for 2a the last step in the catalytic 
cycle shown in Scheme 4 is slower as compared to the other 
allenoates. An active intermediate could be detected by 31P 
NMR during the reaction (for details, see Fig. S7 in SI). In 
summary, the MAA values can reveal that the electrophilicities 
of Michael acceptors effectively influence the overall reaction 
rate; however, the influences of other steps in the the 
multisetp catalytic cycles could not be ignored in some cases.

Conclusions
In conclusion, we have developed a novel tertiary phosphine 
catalyzed [3 + 2] annulation of 2-aminoacrylates with 
allenoates, affording the respective 3-pyrroline derivatives 
under mild conditions. A new type of in situ generated 
ketoimine is applied to construct an amino quaternary 
stereogenic center, which provides a new way of thinking 
about constructing the biologically and pharmacologically 
important 3-pyrroline derivatives. The kinetic profiles and 
the calculation of Methyl Anion Affinity (MAA) values reveal 
that different kinds of allenoates can effectively influence 
the reaction rate. The further studies on the asymmetric 
catalytic version of this reaction are currently underway in our 
laboratory.
Experimental
General experimental method
NMR spectra were recorded with a Bruker spectrometer at 
400 MHz (1H NMR), 100 MHz (13C NMR) and 376 MHz (19F 
NMR) in CDCl3, respectively. Chemical shift were reported in 
ppm down field from internal TMS. Organic solvents used were 
dried by standard methods when necessary. Commercially 
available reagents were used without further purification. All 
reactions were monitored by TLC with Huanghai GF254 silica 
gel coated plates. Flash column chromatography was carried 
out using 300-400 mesh silica gel at increased pressure. 
Infrared spectra were recorded on a Perkin-Elmer PE-983 
spectrometer with absorption in cm-1. Mass spectra were 
recorded by ESI and HRMS was measured on a HP-5989 
instrument.

A convenient and efficient strategy for the synthesis of 3-
pyrrolines containing an amino quaternary stereogenic 
center via phosphine catalyzed formal [3 + 2] annulation 
of allenoates with 2-aminoacrylates is disclosed. The 
reaction is easy to perform in good to excellent yields and 
extend to a gram-scale reaction. The catalytic mechanism 
was investigated by DFT and kinetic studies.
